title: COMMUNITY & CONTENT MANAGER (CANVA + Ai + GHL)
description:
Compensation: $500/month

Schedule: Thursday through Monday, 12:00 PM–8:00 PM Pacific Time

Start Date: Immediately

Hours: 40 hrs/week

Days: 5 days/week

Type: Remote, Non-Exclusive Contractor

Location: Remote



ABOUT THE ROLE



We are looking for a reliable, responsive, and highly organized Community & Content Manager with strong Canva skills to manage the day-to-day activity, content, events, and organization of up to five online communities.



This is first and foremost a community management role. You will be responsible for keeping your assigned communities active, organized, visually polished, current, and running smoothly.



Strong Canva skills are a must. You must also be comfortable using Ai effectively and working within GoHighLevel (GHL).



We are having an interview round TODAY the day this is posted, September 19 in California:

Community & Canva Specialist interviews 9:30 – 10:00am Pacifc





If you have community management and Canva skills, come join!



WHAT YOU'LL DO



You may be responsible for up to five communities at the same time.



Your responsibilities will include:



• Manage day-to-day community activity

• Create, schedule, and publish regular community content

• Maintain content and posting calendars

• Create and maintain community event calendar entries, including images, descriptions, dates, times, and links

• Create Canva graphics for posts, announcements, events, webinars, promotions, and other community activities

• Coordinate community events, webinars, and live sessions

• Post event announcements, reminders, and follow-up content

• Keep pinned posts, resources, links, and community information current

• Monitor community activity and respond to routine questions when appropriate

• Escalate questions or issues requiring specialized attention

• Organize graphics, documents, videos, recordings, templates, links, and other community assets

• Create and maintain logical folder structures and naming conventions

• Keep Canva templates and reusable creative assets organized

• Create, maintain, and follow SOPs for recurring community activities

• Create checklists and repeatable workflows where appropriate

• Make basic updates within GoHighLevel

• Use Ai tools for content, research, images, problem-solving, and productivity

• Follow up on open tasks and make sure things do not fall through the cracks

• Provide a clear handoff when something remains open at the end of your shift



CANVA SKILLS ARE REQUIRED



Canva is a significant part of this position.



You should be able to:



• Create polished community and social graphics

• Create event, webinar, announcement, and promotional graphics

• Work efficiently from existing Canva templates and brand guidelines

• Create new layouts when needed

• Resize and adapt creative for different platforms and formats

• Work effectively with photos, logos, backgrounds, typography, and other visual elements

• Maintain the distinct visual identity of multiple communities

• Organize Canva templates and reusable assets

• Recognize when a design looks cluttered, unbalanced, off-brand, low-quality, or obviously Ai-generated



You do not need to be a professional graphic designer, but you do need to be genuinely good at Canva and have strong visual judgment.



USING Ai WELL



We expect you to be comfortable using modern Ai tools as part of your everyday work.



You should know how to use Ai for:



• Drafting and improving community content

• Repurposing existing content

• Research and brainstorming

• Summarizing source material

• Image generation and editing

• Learning unfamiliar tools

• Problem-solving

• Improving the speed and quality of your work



However, copying and pasting generic Ai-generated content is not acceptable.



Final content should:



• Sound natural and human

• Be clear and conversational

• Be specific rather than abstract

• Match the audience and voice of the individual community

• Avoid unnecessary hype and filler

• Avoid repetitive or formulaic Ai phrasing

• Avoid unnecessary em dashes

• Not read like generic Ai-generated content



We sometimes refer to generic, low-quality Ai-generated writing as "Ai slop." We don't want it.



Ai should make you a better and faster Community Manager. It should not replace your judgment, writing ability, creativity, or understanding of the audience.



CONTENT & EVENT MANAGEMENT



You will be responsible for keeping content and events organized across your assigned communities.



For a typical event, you should be capable of owning the complete workflow:



Event Confirmed → Calendar Entry Created → Graphic Created → Announcement Posted → Reminders Scheduled → Event Supported → Follow-Up Posted



This may include:



• Confirming dates and times

• Creating calendar entries

• Writing event descriptions

• Adding registration, meeting, or webinar links

• Creating Canva graphics

• Publishing announcements

• Scheduling reminders

• Coordinating with hosts and team members

• Making sure required materials are ready

• Supporting event execution

• Publishing recordings, resources, or follow-up content



You should recognize the steps required to successfully execute an event rather than waiting for someone to assign every individual task.



ORGANIZATION & SOP OWNERSHIP



Organization is a major part of this role.



You are not simply expected to locate files, graphics, templates, and other assets. You are expected to create and maintain the organizational structure that makes those things easy for everyone to find and use.



You will:



• Organize graphics, documents, videos, recordings, links, templates, and other digital assets

• Create and maintain logical folder structures

• Establish and follow clear naming conventions

• Keep Canva templates and brand assets organized

• Maintain content and event calendars

• Maintain commonly used links, resources, and reference materials

• Create SOPs for recurring responsibilities

• Follow existing SOPs consistently

• Update SOPs as processes change

• Create checklists for repeatable activities

• Identify recurring activities that should become documented processes

• Keep documentation current enough that another team member could step in and understand what to do



Your communities and their supporting assets should stay organized because you manage them, not because someone else periodically has to clean them up.



GOHIGHLEVEL



You should have working familiarity with GoHighLevel or be capable of becoming productive in it quickly.



Depending on the community, you may be asked to:



• Work within GHL Communities

• Update calendars and events

• Make basic changes to pages or funnels

• Update text, images, links, buttons, or forms

• Work with contacts and other basic GHL functionality

• Follow established GHL workflows and SOPs



We are not hiring a GHL developer. We are looking for a Community Manager who is comfortable operating inside GHL.



RESPONSIVENESS & OWNERSHIP



During your assigned coverage hours, you must be reachable and responsive.



When a request comes in:



Request Received → Acknowledge → Investigate → Handle → Verify → Confirm → Escalate/Handoff if Needed



If you do not immediately know how to accomplish something, investigate it. Use Ai. Review the SOP. Try to solve it.



If something requires specialized expertise or authority you do not have, escalate rather than guess.



During quieter periods, proactively review:



• Your assigned communities

• Upcoming content and posts

• Content calendars

• Upcoming events

• Graphics that need to be prepared

• Calendar accuracy

• Outdated information

• Unanswered questions

• Open tasks and follow-ups

• Asset and folder organization

• SOPs and documentation that need to be created or updated



The role is non-exclusive. You may work with other clients or projects as long as they do not interfere with your responsibilities or responsiveness during assigned coverage hours.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR



We're looking for someone who has:



• Community management experience

• Strong Canva skills

• Strong practical Ai skills

• Working familiarity with GoHighLevel or the ability to learn it quickly

• Strong writing and editing ability

• The ability to recognize and remove poor-quality Ai writing

• Experience managing content calendars

• Experience coordinating online events or webinars

• Strong organizational skills

• Experience organizing digital assets

• Experience creating, maintaining, and following SOPs

• Strong attention to detail

• Good visual judgment

• Strong written communication

• Reliability and responsiveness

• Ability to work independently

• Ability to manage multiple communities without mixing up their brands, audiences, assets, or schedules

• Good judgment about when to solve something independently and when to escalate



APPLICATION QUESTIONS



Please answer all questions clearly in your application:



1. What online communities have you managed, and what were your responsibilities?

2. How many communities or brands have you managed simultaneously?

3. Describe your Canva experience and provide examples of graphics you personally created.

4. Which Ai tools do you regularly use, and how do you use them?

5. How do you prevent Ai-assisted content from sounding generic or obviously Ai-generated?

6. What experience do you have with GoHighLevel?

7. What experience do you have managing content and event calendars?

8. What experience do you have coordinating webinars or online events?

9. How have you organized digital assets, templates, content, or files for a team?

10. Have you created or maintained SOPs? Please provide an example.

11. Are you willing to record short-form videos about various topics, products, and services?

12. Once you have demonstrated that you are effective with short-form video, are you willing to run approximately 45-minute webinars that we have prepared and trained you to deliver?

13. Are you flexible with your schedule and available for a 5-day coverage schedule, including weekends if needed?

14. How soon can you start?



7-DAY EVALUATION PERIOD



All selected candidates will begin with a 7-day evaluation period.



During this period, we will evaluate:



• Community management ability

• Canva capability and visual judgment

• Content quality

• Ability to use Ai without producing generic Ai content

• GHL capability

• Ability to manage multiple communities

• Content and event calendar management

• Event coordination

• Organization

• SOP creation and adherence

• Reliability and responsiveness

• Accuracy and attention to detail

• Proactivity and follow-through

• Communication

• Independent problem-solving

• Judgment about when to handle something and when to escalate



Candidates who successfully demonstrate these capabilities may be offered the opportunity to continue with the team long-term.



THE RIGHT PERSON FOR THIS ROLE



You are a Community Manager first, but you bring a broader skill set than a traditional Community Manager.



You can manage the community, write the post, create the Canva graphic, add the event to the calendar, organize the assets, coordinate the webinar, use Ai intelligently, make a basic GHL update, document the process, and make sure the details don't get missed.



If you are a strong Community Manager who is genuinely good at Canva, comfortable with Ai and GHL, highly organized, responsive, and able to manage multiple communities, we'd like to hear from you.

Job Description:

We're a multi-chain DeFi protocol building LP Bonds, a new liquidity primitive that locks liquidity long-term while keeping user positions tradable. We need Business Development partners who can introduce us to crypto launchpads, DEXs, chains, and established crypto projects.



THE OPPORTUNITY:

 Every successful introduction that leads to a partnership earns you serious money. One good partnership can be worth $5,000-10,000+ as it grows.



COMPENSATION:

Base Pay: $10/hour, 10 hours/week ($100/week). Paid 50% in Ethereum (ETH) and 50% in $GMI tokens on an 18-month vesting schedule, building you a long-term position in the multi-chain $GMI ecosystem.

Minimum Requirement: 1 qualified appointment per week. A qualified appointment means a scheduled call that actually takes place between me and a decision-maker (founder, BD lead, or marketing head) at a crypto launchpad, DEX, chain, or established project, and meets our qualification criteria. Your first qualified appointment each week is covered by your base pay.



Appointment Bonus: Every additional qualified appointment beyond the first pays $100, split 50% ETH and 50% $GMI (same vesting).



Commission: Commission: 25% of all upgrade fees generated by your partnerships for the first 90 days after the partnership goes live, then 10% through month 12. Our 4-level upgrade system means every user your partnership brings in can pay upgrade fees multiple times, and you earn on every single one during your commission window.



Bond Bonuses (based on total dollar value of bonds minted through your partnerships):

+$500 when $10,000 is reached

+$1,000 when $20,000 is reached

+$5,000 when $100,000 is reached, and another +$5,000 for every additional $100,000. No ceiling.

Bonuses are cumulative. Hit $100,000 minted and you've collected $6,500 in bonuses total. Every $100,000 after that adds another $5,000.



Note: A successful partnership means a project you introduced signs the LP Bonds integration agreement and goes live on our marketplace. You book the qualified call, I run the deal and close it.

Hunger to earn based on results, not hours



YOU DON'T NEED:

THE ROLE:

 Your job is booking qualified calls. You reach into your network, find decision-makers at crypto projects, and get them on a scheduled call with me. I close the deals, you collect appointment bonuses, commissions, and bond bonuses as your partnerships go live and grow.

Example: ONE solid launchpad partnership that mints $100,000 in bonds earns you $6,500 in bond bonuses, and with thousands of bondholders paying upgrade fees, your 25% commission pushes your total past $8,000.

Ready to turn your crypto connections into serious income?

 handle

title: Crypto Business Development Manager | Partnerships & Appointment Setting

How to apply

Applications missing any item are auto-rejected. Send:



1. Loom video (2-3 min): who you are, your crypto experience, the most qualified appointments you've personally booked in one month, and how you'd produce 5 qualified GMI partnership calls per week.

2. In writing (3-4 sentences): what a launchpad is and why one would want LP Bonds for its projects.

3. Scenario: "Your reps sent 250 targeted messages in one week, received 18 positive replies, and booked zero qualified calls. What do you inspect, and what do you change in the next 48 hours?"

4. One target for GMI (a DEX, launchpad, or ecosystem): why it's qualified, the exact role you'd contact, the channel, and the personalized first message you'd send.

5. Your
 handle, available hours in GMT+8, and earliest start date.



Subject line must start with: BOND OPS





At target pace this role pays roughly $1,500 to $2,500/month depending on how many appointments you book personally vs through your reps, with no cap on the upside. Base is the floor, not the offer.



About GMI

GonnaMakeIt (GMI) built LP Bonds, a live DeFi liquidity product deployed across 9+ EVM chains (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and more).

LP Bonds lock liquidity for 20 years while giving users a tradeable Bond NFT earning
% APR. The liquidity is locked, the user is not: they can sell their Bond NFT anytime. Rewards accrue inside the bond instead of being farmed and dumped.

Our partnership targets: DEXs, token launchpads, L1/L2 blockchain ecosystems, and select token projects with strong strategic fit.

We need someone to build and run a BD engine that consistently puts qualified partnership calls on the founder's calendar.





The role

One job: produce qualified partnership calls that actually happen, every week.



The founder takes the calls and closes. You own everything before that: rep recruiting and management, target selection, qualification, outreach strategy, follow-up, pipeline, booking, call prep, and funnel diagnosis.



This is a player-coach role. You manage commission-based BD reps AND personally do outreach and book calls whenever the team is below target. Meetings, training, recruiting, and spreadsheet work do not count as output. Qualified calls held count as output.





The metric



Qualified partnership appointments held per week. After ramp: floor 2, target 5, strong 6+.



A call counts only when ALL are true: the target passes our qualification standard, the attendee is a decision-maker (or credible sponsor with direct access to one), they explicitly expressed interest in LP Bonds for their org, they know what the call is about, the call happens, a real partnership discussion occurs, and the founder confirms it was qualified.



Does NOT count: no-shows, reschedules until held, calls where they pitch their product to us, generic networking, community mods who can't advance a deal, duplicates, or projects that can't realistically use LP Bonds.





What you own

1. Rep performance. Audit the existing rep team immediately. Recruit replacements as needed. Give each rep target accounts, messaging, channels, and weekly numbers. Coach producers, cut non-producers. A rep showing no meaningful pipeline progress after 10 working days gets diagnosed and acted on, not carried for 30.

2. Targeting. At least 80% of the active pipeline is DEXs, launchpads, and L1/L2 ecosystems. Targets are EVM-compatible unless the founder approves an exception. Do not fill the pipeline with projects just because they're easy to reach.

3. Qualification. You run (or audit) our LP Bonds Partner Assessment on every interested project. Score of 5/10+ passes to the founder. Below 5 can be escalated for founder review if you believe it's a real opportunity. Before any prospect reaches the founder you confirm: real scale/traction, a genuine LP Bonds fit, a decision-maker in the loop, and explicit interest in LP Bonds for THEM. "We want to explore this for our ecosystem" is interest. "Sounds cool, let's find synergies" is not.

4. Conversion, not volume. Our history shows the exact failure you're hired to prevent: reps sending 40-60 outreaches a week, reporting "interested projects," and producing no decision-maker conversations and no calls. You own the conversion at every stage:

A. Positive reply ? meaningful advancement within 5 business days. That means a decision-maker conversation, a
 group or direct thread with the right person, or a concrete scheduled next step toward a call. If none occurs, the prospect is recycled or closed out of active pipeline. Claimed interest that never advances counts as nothing.

B. Every live opportunity has one owner, one next action, one deadline.

C. Any opportunity untouched for 5 business days gets a decision: advance, recycle, or close. Nothing sits in "waiting."

D. "Calendly shared" is not a completed task. No booking within 2 business days means follow-up happens, and the prospect is told to confirm the booking with both you and the rep.

E. If significant outreach produces no qualified calls, you identify the failure point (targets, contacts, messaging, channel, follow-up, or rep) and launch a new test within 24 hours. The same broken approach never runs for multiple weeks.



5. Pipeline control. One accurate source of truth: target, category, tier, contact and decision-maker status, owner, every touch, stage, next action, deadline, call status. Duplicate outreach prevented. All partner groups remain accessible to GMI even if a rep leaves.

6. Founder handoff. Before a call goes on the founder's calendar: a short brief covering who they are, why they're qualified, why LP Bonds fit, what interest they expressed, who d
, and the desired outcome. No Calendly shared before the qualification gate is complete.

7. Reporting and escalation. Every Friday YOU post one consolidated report: outreach sent, positive replies, qualified conversations, groups created, calls booked, calls held, conversion at each stage, per-rep results, stalled deals, next week's tests. Exact numbers and names, no narratives. Chasing reps for their numbers is your job, done before Friday, never visible to the founder.

If the week is heading to zero qualified calls, you tell the founder THAT DAY with the likely cause, the numbers, the fix being launched, and when results should show. Bad news early is rewarded. Bad news buried is a dealbreaker.



Time allocation

A. 50%+ on outreach, follow-up, and appointment conversion

B. Up to 25% managing and recruiting reps

C. Up to 25% research, reporting, and admin



Building internal tools, assigning books, refining meeting formats, and polishing trackers do not count toward anything. If the team is below target, your personal outreach time goes up.





First 30 days (paid trial)

Day 3: Full audit of every rep and the current pipeline. Immediate correction plan presented. 

Day 7: Clean pipeline and reporting system live. 100+ prioritized qualified targets. Every rep assigned accounts and numbers. Two outreach tests launched. Your personal outreach started. 

Day 14: 2+ qualified appointments held. Measurable conversion at each funnel stage. Non-performers cut or on a final clock. Zero held appointments by Day 14 triggers an immediate role review. 

Day 30 minimum: 6 qualified appointments held, 2+ in the final week, clean pipeline, producing rep core. Target: 8-10 held, exiting at a 3-5/week pace.



Hit the numbers and this grows into a larger BD leadership role with more hours and higher comp as we scale.



Compensation

A. Base: $10/hr, up to 20 hrs/week

B. $100 for every qualified appointment held that you personally booked

C. $30 override for every qualified appointment held that your reps booked

Partnership revenue, two lanes:

D. Partnerships YOU originated: you earn the full rep-tier package: 25% of upgrade fees for the first 90 days after go-live, then 10% through month 12, plus the bond bonus ladder (+$500 at $10K minted, +$1,000 at $20K, +$5,000 at $100K and every $100K after, cumulative, no ceiling).

E. Partnerships your REPS originated: you earn an override equal to 20% of your rep's commission payouts, paid by GMI on top of their commission, never deducted from them, plus $250 per partnership once $2,500 in cumulative LP Bond value has been minted in that partner's pools (USD value at time of mint, verified on-chain).

Every partnership has exactly one originator of record in our tracker, so lanes never stack on the same deal.

F, Additional bonuses possible for exceptional strategic partnerships

G. No cap on any of the above. One appointment bonus per call ($100 personal OR $30 override, not both)

H. Appointment bonuses paid after the call happens and the founder confirms it met the standard

I. Base and bonuses paid 50/50 in ETH and GMI, exact valuation method provided in writing before you start 





Requirements

A. Crypto-native: DEXs, launchpads, liquidity, TVL, ecosystems, no googling required

B. Prior crypto BD, partnerships, lead-gen, or appointment-setting experience with calls you personally booked

C. Experience managing contractors or reps against numbers, and comfortable cutting non-performers

D. Excellent written English, comfortable messaging founders and senior decision-makers

E. Organized: CRMs, trackers,
, X, LinkedIn, email, outreach platforms (we use Saleshandy)

F. 3+ hrs daily overlap with GMT+7/+8

G. Responsive within 10 minutes during your agreed working block unless on a scheduled call





Working standards

Outcomes over activity. Calls held over calls promised. Decision-makers over moderators. Explicit interest over vague networking. Exact numbers over narratives. Problems escalated the day they appear. Every opportunity has an owner, a next action, and a deadline. No hiding bad weeks. No perfecting systems that don't produce calls. The founder never manages your reps.

title: We're Hiring: Full-Time Video Editor!
description:
About Us

Alien Prints is a fast-growing custom apparel company based in Addison, Illinois. We produce 200+ orders per month of screen-printed, embroidered, and DTF-transferred custom apparel for construction companies, service businesses, and organizations across the US.



We're searching for a creative and detail-oriented Full-Time Video Editor who can turn ideas into engaging visual content. From social media clips to marketing campaigns, you'll play a key role in creating videos that captivate audiences and elevate our brand.



Job Requirements: Must have

• Strong understanding of hooks, pacing, captions, and trending formats

Your job is to edit these into short-form and long-form videos optimized for each platform.



This is a high-volume role. You will produce 8–15 edited video pieces per day across different formats. Speed, consistency, and understanding of what makes content perform on social media are essential.



What you will do

Short-form video editing (primary focus — 70% of time)

• Edit raw clips into 15–60 second videos for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts

• Add captions/subtitles to all videos (burned-in, styled, readable)

• Write and add text hooks in the first 1–2 seconds of every video

• Add transitions, zoom effects, and pacing that match platform trends

• Select and sync trending audio/music where appropriate

• Create satisfying loop videos from production process footage (press pulls, ink shots, transfer peels)

• Edit before/after reveal videos with dramatic transitions

• Format and resize the same video for different platforms (9:16, 1:1, 16:9)



Long-form video editing (20% of time)

• Edit 1 long-form YouTube video per week (5–15 minutes)

• Full process walkthroughs: a single order from design to shipping

• Educational content: print method comparisons, branding guides, industry tips

• Add intro/outro, lower thirds, chapter markers, and b-roll where needed

• Create compelling thumbnails for YouTube videos



Ad creative (10% of time)

• Edit short video ads for Meta 
/Instagram) campaigns

• Create multiple variations of the same ad for A/B testing

• Follow direct creative briefs from the Content Manager



Daily output expectations

• 8–10 short-form videos (TikTok/Reels/Shorts format) per day

• 2–3 Stories-format clips per day

• 1 long-form YouTube video per week

• 1–2 ad creatives per week

title: Content Writer, Health and Wellness

.

Daily output, building over the first month. Quality first, then speed.

Two links to articles you wrote that are published online, at least one on a health, science or nutrition topic.

Review every case individually before responding

Analyze the customer's claim, order history, tracking, fulfillment, and communication

Verify live carrier tracking and delivery information

Handle split shipments and multiple tracking numbers correctly

Collect and organize all relevant evidence

Build clear timelines showing order → shipment → delivery → customer communication

Write professional, factual, and convincing PayPal responses

Significantly Not as Described

Partial/split shipments

Multiple tracking numbers

Delivered orders disputed by customers

Refund and return disagreements

Other common PayPal buyer disputes

This position can start immediately.

Your availability and how soon you can start

title: Instagram Content Clipper, Editor & Poster — 2 Coaching Business Pages (Daily)
description:
We run a personal branding / coaching business (Done4U), and we're hiring ONE reliable, experienced content VA to run TWO business Instagram accounts: 



1) Our official Done4U business page — a page built on PROOF: testimonials, client wins, and our best coaching moments.

2) A second content account for our business partner Jake 
 — a higher-volume educational page: clipped YouTube, raw "yaps," and talking-head reels. 



Both pages represent our brand. Everything posted has to look sharp, consistent, and on-brand — every single post. This is a strict, high-standard role with clear SOPs for both accounts. Read carefully. If you skim job posts, miss details, or need hand-holding on every cut, this is not for you.



WHO THIS IS FOR:

This is a taste-driven, experience-required role. You must already know how to clip long-form content down into short-form — pulling the perfect 30–60 seconds out of a 90-minute call or a full-length YouTube video. You should instantly recognise a hook, a moment, and a payoff worth posting. You must also be a genuinely capable editor.



WHAT YOU'LL DO (daily, across both accounts):

- Go through our raw footage (
 / Google Drive) and pull the strongest moments.

- Clip and edit cleanly in CapCut: trim tight, add clear captions, crop to vertical 9:16 (and 16:9 where briefed), and keep a consistent premium look.

- Done4U page: log in and post 2–3 clips per day, mixing content types, following the SOP.

- Jake's 2nd account: produce a steady volume of clips across three styles — (A) YouTube clipped up, (B) raw yaps, (C) talking-head reels — matching locked brand fonts, colours, and caption styles, and post/schedule when approved.

- Keep simple trackers updated so nothing is ever posted twice.



THE CONTENT YOU'LL BE CLIPPING:

- Mastermind sessions, 1:1 coaching calls, and community coaching calls

- Full YouTube videos from two accounts — clipping the best moments from across the whole video, not just the intros

- Talking-head / piece-to-camera footage and raw "yaps"

- Occasionally a coach's content (in the form of community calls and YT moments)



NON-NEGOTIABLES — you MUST:

- Have real, proven experience clipping long-form footage into short-form (SEND EXAMPLES TO BE CONSIDERED).

- Be a strong editor in CapCut — captions, trimming, text, basic keyframes/zoom, vertical + landscape export.

- Have genuine taste — you know what's worth posting and what isn't.

- Be comfortable logging into Instagram and posting 2–3 times a day, every day, following an SOP exactly.

- Follow written brand locks precisely — fonts, colours, caption styles, safe zones. No inventing your own look.

- Be proactive and self-sufficient — use the SOPs, figure things out, and only ask when it genuinely matters. We do not have time for a hundred questions a day.

- Treat the brand as sacred — image, structure, and consistency come first, always. Every post must look like it belongs to the same premium page.

- Be reliable, detail-oriented, and consistent. This is a daily role and misses get noticed.

- Have a laptop/phone that can edit and export 1080×1920 and 1920×1080 without crashing, plus stable internet. Comfortable with 
, Instagram, and Google Sheets.



TIMEZONE: We often work to Asia/Dubai (UTC+4). State your timezone and daily working window.



WHAT YOU GET:

- $3 USD/hour, with raises based on performance.

- Full SOPs and clear direction for both accounts — you'll know exactly what to look for.

- A steady, long-term role for the right person.



Honest note: $3/hr is an entry rate and we're upfront about it (there is potential for raises with performance - we are looking for long term team members)

title: Director of Business Operations and Systems
description:
DIRECTOR OF BUSINESS OPERATIONS AND SYSTEMS

WORK SETUP: Fully remote and full time

EXPERIENCE: 5 years above

REPORTS TO: Owner

COMPENSATION: $500/week



Position Summary



High Meadows Resorts is developing a luxury destination property in Ellicottville, New York, with 17 rental villas, a full-service restaurant, and an event center serving banquet, corporate gatherings, wellness retreats, celebrations, and group stays.



We are seeking a senior hospitality operator to build the commercial and operating foundation before opening and strengthen it as the business grows. This person will own business development, financial models, operating systems, software integration, workforce planning, and team adherence to agreed processes. The role works directly with the owner and must be comfortable testing assumptions, identifying risk, and recommending better options with clear financial and operational reasoning.



Key Responsibilities



Business Development and Commercial Planning

•Build and maintain pro formas for the restaurant, villas, event center, and related revenue opportunities. Models should cover demand, pricing, occupancy, average daily rate, food and labor costs, fixed costs, cash flow, and break-even scenarios.

•Develop budgets, forecasts, pricing recommendations, and management dashboards with clear assumptions and measurable targets.

•Create partnership, referral, group sales, and event pipelines with defined stages, owners, follow-up standards, conversion measures, and booked revenue reporting.



Operating Systems and Guest Journey

•Map and improve the full guest journey from inquiry and booking through pre-arrival, check-in, stay, issue recovery, check-out, and post-stay follow-up.

•Create SOPs, checklists, handoffs, approval limits, quality controls, and escalation paths for reservations, housekeeping, maintenance, dining, events, and guest services.

•Establish system governance through assigned owners, version control, training records, compliance reviews, exception reporting, and regular improvement cycles.



Technology and Software Integration

•Define requirements and lead vendor evaluation for the website, booking engine, property management system, channel manager, CRM, point-of-sale, payments, accounting, guest messaging, housekeeping, workforce scheduling, and analytics tools.

•Design the integration map for data flow, permissions, ownership, reporting, handoffs, and failure contingencies.

•Coordinate configuration, testing, training, staff acceptance, and launch readiness with internal owners and external vendors.



Workforce Planning and Operating Discipline

•Develop the organization structure, role definitions, manpower plan, housekeeping turnover model, shift schedules, coverage rules, and labor forecasts.

•Track pre-opening dependencies, decisions, risks, and deadlines across lodging, dining, events, facilities, finance, and marketing.

•Coach managers on how each system should be used, verify adherence through operating reviews, and challenge leadership respectfully when evidence or unit economics do not support a proposed approach.



Required Qualifications



•More than 5 years of progressive experience in business development, operations, systems, and protocols.

•Demonstrated financial fluency in pro formas, P&L management, budgeting, forecasting, pricing, labor modeling, and performance reporting.

•Proven experience building SOPs, controls, workflows, and accountability systems and achieving sustained team adoption.

•Experience in business software. Programming is not required, but the candidate must understand requirements, data, testing, implementation, and vendor management.

•Strong written and spoken English, executive-level communication, and the ability to work independently while maintaining reliable overlap with U.S. Eastern Time.



Paid Trial and Hiring Process



Shortlisted finalists will be invited to a paid trial lasting one to two weeks under a written scope before either party makes a long-term commitment. The assignment may include a focused restaurant pro forma, guest check-in workflow, software integration map, KPI dashboard, or short operating plan using information supplied by the company.

Evaluation will focus on commercial reasoning, systems design, prioritization, constructive challenge, execution quality, communication, and working fit.



How to Apply



Apply through the platform where this vacancy is posted. Include your resume, a short note explaining why the role fits your background, and one anonymized work sample such as a pro forma, operating dashboard, SOP, systems map, or pre-opening plan.

•Describe one system you built or repaired, how you gained team adoption, and the measurable result.

•Describe one occasion when you challenged a senior leader's assumption and how the decision was resolved.

•State your earliest available start date, expected U.S. Eastern Time overlap, and compensation expectations.



We are looking for a senior operator who can help leadership make sound decisions and build an organization that performs consistently before and after opening.

title: Insight-Led Content Researcher & Scriptwriter - Psychology
description:
**Part-Time | Remote | Long-Term Opportunity**



We are looking for someone who is unusually good at finding **interesting ideas hidden inside stories**.



This is not a traditional copywriting role.



It is not a social-media VA role.



And we are not looking for someone who simply takes a topic and asks ChatGPT to write a script about it.



Your job is to find stories, contradictions, behaviours and business decisions that make someone think:



**“I've never thought about it like that before.”**



The subject could come from almost anywhere:



* Psychology and human behaviour

* Relationships

* Business and entrepreneurship

* Famous companies and brands

* Celebrity and internet culture

* Sport

* Status and ambition

* Money

* History

* Technology

* Crime

* Advertising

* Strange cultural trends

* Unexpected success or failure stories



The industry matters less than whether there is a **strong idea underneath the story**.



## The Type of Content We Create



For example:



Kim Kardashian's story can become a script about how scandal changed from something that destroyed fame into something that can manufacture it.



Ferrari having hundreds of millions of fans but relatively few customers can become a script about how people who never buy your product can still increase its value.



Home Depot filling its early stores with empty paint cans can become a script about how perception influences whether customers trust a new business.



A chaotic relationship can become a script about how the person creating your anxiety can also become the person you depend on for relief.



Someone surviving extreme violence but being terrified to apologise to their father can become a script about how people often choose difficult things that preserve control while avoiding the difficult thing that removes it.



The interesting part is rarely just **what happened**.



The job is finding:



**Why is this interesting?**



**What does this reveal?**



**What is the hidden mechanism?**



**Why would somebody who knows nothing about the original story care?**



## What We Do NOT Want



We are not looking for generic content like:



“5 signs of a toxic relationship.”



“3 ways to grow your business.”



“Why Rolex is successful.”



“Ferrari has a strong brand.”



“Know your worth.”



“Work hard and never give up.”



These are observations anyone could make.



We want the layer underneath the obvious observation.



For example:



Weak:



**“Rolex is successful because people like luxury watches.”**



Better:



**“Scarcity has almost nothing to do with making a small number of products. Rolex can make around a million watches and still create scarcity because demand outruns supply.”**



Weak:



**“Ferrari has a powerful brand.”**



Better:



**“Ferrari's biggest fans may never become customers — but those non-customers help create the cultural status that makes the product valuable to the people who do buy.”**



That difference is the job.



## Your Role



You will own much of the research and early script-development process.



This includes:



* Finding fascinating podcasts, interviews, documentaries, articles, Reddit discussions, company stories and historical examples

* Reviewing long transcripts and source material

* Identifying unusual facts, contradictions and stories

* Finding the deeper idea underneath the obvious story

* Researching additional supporting evidence where necessary

* Developing strong hooks

* Turning the strongest ideas into short-form scripts

* Checking our existing script library to avoid repeating ideas we have already covered

* Adding completed scripts to Notion for final review



You can use **ChatGPT, Claude and other AI tools heavily**.



We actively expect you to.



But AI is not the skill we're hiring for.



The valuable skill is knowing when the AI has produced something obvious, boring or fake-deep — and being able to push past it.



## The Most Important Skill: Taste



We care heavily about your ability to distinguish between:



**An interesting topic**



and



**An interesting idea.**



“Ferrari” is a topic.



“Millions of people who will never own a Ferrari help make Ferrari more valuable to the people who can” is an idea.



“Relationships” is a topic.



“The person causing your anxiety can become the person you depend on for relief” is an idea.



“Success” is a topic.



“Success can be more psychologically destabilising than failure because failure allows you to keep believing happiness is waiting at the next milestone” is an idea.



We want someone who naturally looks for the second version.



## What We're Looking For



Strong candidates may come from backgrounds such as:



* Psychology

* Behavioural science

* Journalism

* Sociology

* Philosophy

* Copywriting

* Documentary research

* Business research

* Content strategy



A degree is not required.



What matters more is:



* Exceptional curiosity

* Strong pattern recognition

* Good judgment about what people will actually find fascinating

* Ability to read or watch something long and find the 2% worth turning into content

* Strong written English

* Ability to simplify complex ideas without making them simplistic

* Ability to find strong evidence and examples

* Comfort using AI tools

* Willingness to reject mediocre ideas rather than forcing every source into a script

* Strong organisation and reliability



## Important



We don't want academic writing.



We don't want corporate LinkedIn writing.



And we don't want scripts that sound as if somebody asked AI:



**“Give me a motivational lesson from this story.”**



For example, instead of:



> “This behaviour represents an anxious-avoidant attachment dynamic caused by intermittent reinforcement.”



We prefer:



> “The person making you anxious can become the same person you depend on for relief.”



Instead of:



> “Strong brands benefit from high levels of social proof.”



We prefer:



> “Ferrari has hundreds of millions of fans who will never buy the car — but those people are part of what makes owning one mean something.”



The research can be sophisticated.



The final idea should feel obvious **only after someone explains it**.



## Hours



This will begin as a small **part-time role**.



Approximately 10** hours per week initially**.



Hours can increase substantially if the quality of the work is strong.



We are looking for someone who can potentially grow into a long-term role.



## Paid Trial



Shortlisted applicants will complete a **paid trial**.



We will give you:



* Examples of our strongest existing scripts

* Source material such as a transcript, interview or company story

* Access to examples showing the standard we're looking for



You will be asked to:



1. Research the source.

2. Identify several possible angles.

3. Choose what you believe is the strongest one.

4. Explain briefly why.

5. Write one finished short-form script.



We are primarily testing:



* **Taste**

* Research ability

* Pattern recognition

* Ability to find the non-obvious angle

* Hook selection

* Depth of insight

* Writing ability



We are **not** testing whether you can follow a huge prompt perfectly.



We want to see how you think.



## How to Apply



Please include:



1. Your research, writing or relevant educational background.



2. What subjects you naturally spend time researching.



3. One example of a story, company, person or behaviour you think could make a fascinating short-form script — and briefly explain the hidden idea you would explore.



4. Begin your application with the word **“INSIGHT”** so we know you read the full post.



If you naturally consume a story and find yourself thinking:



**“Everyone is focusing on what happened. The interesting part is why it worked that way.”**



you may be a very good fit for this role.

We have a large database of potential development sites. You will work through these properties, research the applicable zoning and development requirements, review the physical characteristics of the land, and estimate the property's potential unit count.



Your analysis will then be used by our team to underwrite the property and determine the appropriate land purchase price.



Responsibilities

Research zoning classifications and permitted residential uses

Determine allowable density and potential townhome unit count

Research setbacks, parking requirements, lot coverage, height limits, minimum lot dimensions, and other development standards

Review GIS maps, parcel maps, assessor information, and public records

Analyze parcel dimensions, shape, road access, easements, and rights-of-way

Identify potential issues involving flood zones, utilities, drainage, topography, or other site constraints

Research city and county zoning ordinances

Evaluate whether a property appears suitable for our townhome development model

Document findings and assumptions clearly

Flag properties that require additional research or professional review

Background We're Looking For



Candidates with backgrounds in any of the following are strongly encouraged to apply:



Geodetic Engineering

Land Surveying

Civil Engineering

GIS / Geospatial Analysis

Zoning

Urban Planning

Land Development

Site Planning



You do not need extensive U.S. real estate experience. We are more interested in finding someone with a strong technical understanding of land who can learn our development process.



Ideal Candidate



You enjoy working with maps, land data, zoning regulations, and technical information.



You are analytical, detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable researching a problem until you find the answer.



Most importantly, you understand that determining development potential requires more than simply looking at acreage. Zoning, density, setbacks, access, easements, parcel configuration, utilities, and other constraints can all affect how many units can actually be built.



This is a long-term opportunity for the right person.



To Apply



Please send a short voice recording introducing yourself and briefly describing your relevant experience.

title: B2B Cold Caller / Appointment Setter – Healthcare Services
description:
# B2B Cold Caller / Appointment Setter – Healthcare Services



**Remote | Part-Time | 20–25 Hours/Week**



We are a mobile phlebotomy company serving healthcare providers, senior communities, home health organizations, medical practices, laboratories, and other healthcare organizations throughout Michigan.



We are looking for an **experienced B2B Cold Caller / Appointment Setter** to introduce our services to prospective business clients and help us develop new partnerships.

Your primary responsibility will be **outbound calling and business development.** You should be comfortable making a high volume of calls every day and speaking confidently with office managers, administrators, physicians' offices, laboratory representatives, home health agencies, senior living facilities, and other healthcare organizations.



### What You'll Do



* Make a high volume of outbound B2B cold calls

* Contact hundreds of prospective companies and healthcare organizations

* Introduce US Mobile Lab and clearly explain our services

* Identify the appropriate decision-maker within each organization

* Navigate receptionists and gatekeepers professionally

* Ask questions to determine whether the organization could benefit from our services

* Generate qualified leads and schedule follow-up conversations

* Follow up with interested prospects by phone and

* Maintain accurate notes and update lead status

* Build and organize prospect lists when necessary

* Learn our services well enough to have a natural conversation instead of simply reading a script



### Who We're Looking For



**Excellent spoken English is REQUIRED.**



You must be able to communicate clearly, naturally, and professionally with U.S.-based businesses.



The ideal candidate has:



* Highly fluent or near-native spoken English

* Strong, easy-to-understand pronunciation

* Previous **cold-calling, telesales, appointment-setting, or B2B sales experience**

* Confidence speaking with business owners, managers, and healthcare professionals

* The ability to sound conversational rather than scripted

* Experience handling objections and getting past gatekeepers

* Strong phone presence and personality

* Persistence without being overly aggressive

* Ability to make a large number of calls consistently

* Good organizational and follow-up skills

* Reliable internet and a quiet, professional calling environment



Healthcare sales experience is a plus, but **strong cold-calling ability is more important.**



### What Success Looks Like



We are not looking for someone who simply completes a certain number of calls.



We want someone who can turn cold prospects into conversations.



You should be comfortable hearing "no," continuing to the next prospect, following up consistently, and figuring out how to reach the right decision-maker.



Our goal is to introduce US Mobile Lab to **hundreds of potential partner organizations** and develop long-term business relationships.



### Schedule



Approximately **20–25 hours per week**, primarily during U.S. Eastern Time business hours.



### Compensation



Starting compensation will depend on experience and demonstrated cold-calling ability.



There may also be opportunities for **performance-based bonuses for qualified appointments or new accounts generated.**



### IMPORTANT – How to Apply



Please include:



1. Your previous cold-calling or appointment-setting experience.

2. Approximately how many outbound calls you are comfortable making per day.

3. What types of businesses or industries you have called previously.

4. A **30–60 second voice recording** introducing yourself and explaining why you would be a good fit for this position.



Applicants selected for an interview will be asked to perform a short **mock cold call** so we can evaluate communication skills, confidence, objection handling, and overall phone presence.

title: Zoning & Land Development Analyst – GIS / Geodetic / Civil Engineering
description:
We are a U.S.-based real estate development company looking for a Zoning & Land Development Analyst to help us evaluate land for new townhome developments.



Your primary job will be to answer one important question:



How many townhomes can we realistically build on this property?



We have a large master list of potential development properties. You will research each property, analyze its zoning and physical characteristics, and determine its preliminary development potential.



Once we know the estimated number of buildable units, our team can underwrite the property and determine what we can afford to pay for the land.



What You'll Do

Research zoning and permitted uses for each property

Determine allowable residential density and potential number of townhome units

Research setbacks, lot coverage, height limits, parking requirements, minimum lot sizes, and other development standards

Review GIS and parcel maps

Review property boundaries, dimensions, access, easements, rights-of-way, and other potential constraints

Identify flood zones, utilities, topography, and other issues that may affect development

Review city/county zoning codes, development standards, maps, and public records

Estimate a preliminary buildable unit count based on our standardized townhome design

Clearly document your research, assumptions, and conclusions

Flag properties that require additional professional or municipal confirmation

Work through a high volume of properties from our master mailing list

Ideal Background



We are especially interested in candidates with experience or education in:



Geodetic Engineering / Land Surveying

Civil Engineering

GIS / Mapping

Zoning or Land Use

Urban Planning

Land Development / Site Planning

Development Feasibility



Experience working with U.S. properties is a plus, but not required. We can teach you our process and the specific markets we work in.



Who We're Looking For



You should be analytical, highly detail-oriented, comfortable researching technical information, and good at reading maps, parcel information, surveys, and development standards.



You should also be able to work independently, stay organized, communicate clearly, and know when something needs additional review rather than making assumptions.



This is not a sales position. It is a focused research and analysis role for someone who enjoys land, maps, zoning, engineering, and solving development problems.



If you have worked as a Geodetic Engineer, Land Surveyor, GIS Analyst, Zoning Technician, Civil Engineer, or similar technical role, we would especially like to hear from you.



To Apply



Please send us a short voice recording introducing yourself and briefly explaining your relevant experience.

title: CRO Specialist – Deep Audit of 200+ Session Replays (Shopify Store, Ad-to-Purchase Journey)
description:
Hi! I run a DTC e-commerce brand on Shopify and most of our traffic comes from paid ads (Meta). I'm recording hundreds of session replays on our store (over 200 so far) and I need someone to watch them properly and tell me exactly where and why visitors get lost after clicking an ad.



This is an important role. I am NOT looking for someone who runs everything through AI and sends back a generic checklist. I'm looking for a person who actually watches the sessions, takes notes, spots patterns and backs every recommendation with real evidence.



WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Watch and analyze 200+ session replays recorded with Microsoft Clarity and Propel

- Map the real customer journey: ad click > landing page > product page > cart > checkout

- Check if the site keeps the promise of our ads (same message, same offer, same visual feel). I will share our current ads and a description of our typical customer

- Identify friction points: confusion, rage clicks, dead clicks, drop-offs, hesitation, missing information, trust issues, mobile problems

- Tell us what to change: copy, layout, flow, and where better graphics or visuals are needed



WHAT YOU WILL DELIVER

A written audit (Google Doc or similar) with:

1. The top issues, ranked by expected impact on conversions

2. For each issue: replay links + timestamps showing it, how often it happens, why it matters

3. A concrete recommendation for each issue (what to change and where)

4. A short section on ad-to-site consistency: where the site breaks the expectations created by the ads

5. Quick wins vs bigger changes, with a rough effort estimate



REQUIREMENTS

- Proven experience with CRO / UX audits on e-commerce (Shopify is a plus)

- Real experience analyzing session recordings and heatmaps (Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar or similar)

- Understanding of paid traffic and how ad messaging affects landing page behavior

- Strong written English and the ability to explain WHY, not just WHAT

- Patience and attention to detail: this job is about watching carefully, not about speed



HOW WE WORK

- Project-based, with the possibility of ongoing work if the audit is good

- Shortlisted candidates will first do a PAID TEST: analyze 10 replays and send us their top 3 findings



MANDATORY SELECTION TEST - APPLICATIONS WITHOUT THIS WILL BE IGNORED



To prove you read the whole post, START YOUR SUBJECT LINE WITH "REPLAY AUDIT -" followed by your name. Applications without it will not be opened.



Then answer these 4 questions IN YOUR OWN WORDS (AI-generated answers are easy to spot and will be rejected):



1. Describe ONE real finding you discovered by watching session recordings for a past client or project. What was the problem, what did you recommend, and what changed after?

2. A visitor arrives on a product page from a
 ad on mobile, scrolls a little, stops for 8 seconds, then leaves. What would you look at in that replay to understand why, and what could the possible causes be?

3. How would you organize the analysis of 200+ replays so you don't miss patterns? Be specific (tagging, segments, filters, notes).

4. Have you used Microsoft Clarity before? Which other tools have you used for session replays and heatmaps?



Please also include:

- 1-2 examples of audits or CRO reports you have done (links or screenshots, confidential data can be hidden)

- Your availability and how many days you need for the full audit

- Your rate for the full project



Thank you, I look forward to finding the right person!

About the Role:

I am looking for a reliable, creative, and detail-oriented Short-Form Video Editor from the Philippines to help edit engaging videos for my brand.

Our content follows a specific, consistent format: split-screen / top-and-bottom videos featuring Omegle video interactions on the top screen and musicians/performers on the bottom screen.

This is a part-time position (3 shorts per week) with the potential to transition into a full-time role with long-form YouTube editing in the near future.

Key Responsibilities:

Edit 3 short-form videos per week (50 to 80 seconds each).

Synchronize split-screen visuals (Top: Omegle clip / Bottom: Music video or performance clip).

Add dynamic captions/subtitles, sound effects (SFX), clean transitions, and visual hooks to maintain high audience retention.

Ensure audio levels are properly balanced (dialogue vs. background music).

Follow a consistent template and brand style while maintaining fast turnaround times.

Requirements:

Proven experience editing short-form content for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts.

High proficiency in Premiere Pro, CapCut (Desktop), or DaVinci Resolve.

Strong sense of pacing, timing, and audio sync (especially with musical elements).

Great eye for captions/subtitles, typography, and motion graphic overlays.

Stable high-speed internet connection and a reliable work setup.

Good communication skills and ability to meet weekly deadlines consistently.

Compensation & Work Hours:

Starting Rate: $350 USD / month (Part-time output: 3 short-form videos/week).

Payment Frequency: Bi-weekly or monthly (via Wise or PayPal).

Growth: Opportunities for pay increases, long-form content work, and full-time hours as the channel grows.

How to Apply:

If you’re interested, please send an application with the subject line: "Music & Omegle Editor – [Your Name]"

Please include:

Portfolio / Video Links: 3–5 examples of short-form videos you have edited (especially split-screen, music-focused, or dialogue/caption-heavy content).

Editing Tools: What editing software do you use?

Turnaround Time: How long does it usually take you to finish one 60-second edited short?

title: Meta Ads Campaign Specialist with GoHighLevel Expertise
description:
DO NOT APPLY Unless you have multiple years of hands-on media buying experience, strong GoHighLevel expertise, consider yourself an A-player, and are ready to work full-time **exclusively** with us—NOT while managing other clients’ accounts.



We partner with medical practices and doctors to build dominant digital presences through strategic content and paid advertising. We capture high-quality video content in quarterly shoots and transform that raw footage into organic posts and high-converting video ads that position our clients as the leading authorities in their medical markets.



We’re now expanding our team to meet growing demand. I’m looking for a long-term Meta Ads Campaign Specialist with GoHighLevel expertise who can take ownership of campaign performance, the systems supporting lead follow-up, and creative strategy in partnership with our Creative Lead.



Requirements:

• Multiple years of proven experience launching, managing, and optimizing
/Meta ads

• Medical-practice advertising experience is strongly preferred

• Strong understanding of campaign structure

• Strong understanding of funnels (ad, lead, conversion) and performance metrics (CPL, CPA, ROI)

• Hands-on GoHighLevel experience, including workflows, pipelines, forms, calendars, lead routing, and SMS/email automations

• Ability to troubleshoot Meta-to-GoHighLevel lead flow and clearly explain technical issues

• Understanding of hooks, audience psychology, creative testing, and direct-response strategy

• Ability to follow structure and improve existing campaigns

• Experience working in a social media or content agency is a significant plus

• Fluent English with excellent grammar and strong client communication skills

• Extreme attention to detail, consistency, and reliability



Role & Responsibilities:

• Communicate and collaborate through Asana and Slack

• Attention to detail (include your zodiac sign in the subject line!)

• Launch
 ad campaigns quickly, then test and optimize continuously based on our SOPs

• Set up campaigns, ad sets, targeting, and budgets

• Duplicate, pause, or delete campaigns where necessary

• Take ownership of campaign performance from launch through optimization

• Manage the GoHighLevel workflows, pipelines, and follow-up systems supporting campaigns

• Monitor the full funnel from lead to booked appointment and identify bottlenecks

• Troubleshoot Meta and GoHighLevel issues and make quick, informed adjustments

• Work across multiple fast-growing brands

• Remain responsive and communicative on Slack during EST working hours

• Join client calls when needed to clearly explain Meta or GoHighLevel issues



Creative Strategy and Ownership:

• Work under our Creative Lead to analyze campaign performance, identify creative bottlenecks, and recommend new hooks, angles, concepts, and iterations

• Turn account data into clear creative briefs and collaborate with the creative team to produce stronger ads

• Proactively identify what needs to change and bring solutions instead of waiting to be told what to do

• Take responsibility for results while collaborating closely with the Creative Lead and the rest of the team



Rate and Work Schedule:

• Full-time position

• $6–$8 per hour, depending on experience

• Must be available and responsive during Eastern Standard Time working hours

• Long-term opportunity for the right person

• Compensation and responsibilities may increase over time as the role grows



Why Join Us?

You’ll be on the ground floor of helping our clients grow amazing businesses. Having had challenging bosses in the past, I’ve dedicated my career to creating a respectful, supportive, and growth-focused environment. You’ll be highly valued, and together, we’ll push each other to improve.



This role offers room to grow into a senior media buying, creative strategy, or marketing management position. As the business grows, your responsibilities and compensation can grow with it—as long as you consistently produce results and put in the work required for our clients to succeed.



What We Value Most:

• 100% honesty and integrity

• Strong work ethic, including discipline, accountability, and consistency

• A proactive A-player mindset

• Continuous desire to improve

• Asking questions and seeking clarification when needed

• Ability to follow step-by-step instructions and SOPs accurately

• A self-starter mindset and fearlessness in learning and helping

• Ownership: we want someone who finds solutions and keeps accounts moving forward without constant direction



How to Apply:

1. Send a short introduction video.

2. Share your portfolio showcasing relevant work.

3. Send your resume, with references if possible.

4. Tell me about a campaign that failed. What happened, and what did you do?

5. Explain how you scale a winning campaign.

6. Share a screen-recorded walkthrough of one or two Meta ad accounts you’ve managed. Explain how you evaluate performance, identify problems, and d
 what to change.

7. Share a walkthrough of one or two GoHighLevel automations you’ve built. Explain how they are structured and what business problem they solve.

8. Explain what other clients or work you currently have and exactly how you would end or transition those commitments before accepting this full-time position.

9. A Campaign Strategy Test will be shared separately.



Important:

If you’re not comfortable with the compensation, workload, full-time commitment, or EST schedule, please do not apply. Only apply if you are serious, consistent, experienced, and able to follow instructions.

title: Customer Operations Executive – SAP / Wholesale Customer Service
description:
Customer Operations Executive – SAP / Wholesale Customer Service

Full-time | Remote (Philippines) | USD $230 per week | Mon–Fri 9:00am–5:00pm Australian Eastern Time



A leading international apparel and headwear brand needs an experienced Customer Operations Executive for its remote wholesale customer-service team.



You’ll manage wholesale customer orders end-to-end in SAP and/or EDI, coordinate deliveries, and work closely with sales, logistics, warehouse and finance so orders are accurate, on time, and customers stay informed.



Salary: USD $230 per week

Hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00am–5:00pm Australian Eastern Time (AET)



Key responsibilities

• Enter and manage wholesale customer orders in SAP

• Process and monitor EDI orders

• Track open orders, deliveries and stock delays

• Prepare open-order and delivery-status reports

 Communicate order and delivery updates to wholesale customers

• Work closely with sales, sourcing, logistics, warehouse and finance

• Resolve order discrepancies, delivery issues, short shipments and damaged goods

• Provide invoices, POD and order acknowledgements

• Manage returns per company policies

• Assist with product, pricing and account enquiries

• Troubleshoot customer and B2B platform issues

• Support eCommerce order enquiries when required

• Ensure orders are processed accurately and within deadlines



Must-haves

 Fluent spoken and written English (non-negotiable)

• 1–2+ years customer service, order processing, wholesale operations or similar

• SAP experience highly preferred

• EDI order management highly preferred

• Experience in wholesale, retail, FMCG, fashion or distribution

• Strong Excel and Microsoft Office

• Detail-focused, organised, proactive and reliable

• Able to juggle multiple deadlines and follow up independently

• Comfortable working with sales, warehouse, logistics and finance

• Able to work Australian business hours (9:00am–5:00pm AET) consistently



Performance expectations

• ≥97% order accuracy

• Orders entered within 48 hours of receipt

• Enquiries answered within 24 hours

• Delivery delays communicated before due dates

• Warehouse amendments handled promptly

• Ownership of issues from start to resolution



How to apply

1. Updated CV

2. Short summary of your SAP and/or EDI experience

3. Examples of wholesale or customer-service orders you have managed

4. Earliest start date

5. Confirm you can work Mon–Fri 9:00am–5:00pm AET at USD $230 per week



Fluent English is required. Apply direct via OnlineJobs.
